A project can be improved by contributions from people who may never have met each other, and every contribution—whether it is code, documentation, testing, bug reports, or ideas—can make a difference. I also like that open-source communities give beginners an opportunity to learn by working on real-world projects and interacting with experienced developers.

I believe software freedom is important because users and developers should have the ability to understand, modify, share, and improve the software they depend on. At the same time, I think good open-source culture requires respect, clear communication, constructive feedback, and a willingness to help others.

For me, contributing to FOSS is not only about writing code or getting contributions on a profile. It is about becoming part of a community, learning how large projects are built and maintained, and giving something back to the ecosystem that developers around the world benefit from.
